To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
automatic geometric correction of VHR multispectral images can reach accuracies of 1–2 pixels for the sensor physical model (GCPs extraction) and 0.5–1 pixels for the orthoimage (orthorectification).

(1) automatic GCP extraction from vector roads is possible with near-pixel accuracy; (2) the use of vector roads as reference data is a promising approach for the geometric processing of optical VHR data; and (3) the automatic geometric processing of VHR data is possible with sub-pixel accuracy.
automatic geometric corrections of VHR multispectral satellite images are possible with accuracies of 1.5–1.6 pixels and with image processing times of under one hour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic geometric processing of VHR multispectral images and demonstrates the applicability of the proposed algorithms to a large number of satellite images
the development of a fully automatic image processing pipeline that can be used in a variety of applications.
the development of an automatic geometric correction module for VHR multispectral satellite images that is able to achieve near-pixel accuracy in the absence of GCPs and in a fully automatic manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed automatic geometric corrections algorithm is capable of delivering high quality orthophotos and DEMs with high accuracy and efficiency for VHR multispectral satellite images.
automatic image processing is feasible for both RapidEye and WorldView-2 images.
the automatic geometric correction module of STORM is capable of delivering high quality orthoimages for VHR multispectral data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed automatic geometric correction algorithm is capable of delivering sub-pixel accuracies on VHR multispectral satellite images.
automatic processing of VHR multispectral data is possible with accuracies comparable to manual methods and with acceptable processing times.
the automatic geometric processing module of STORM is capable of delivering map-ready orthophotos for multispectral VHR images with accuracies that are sufficient for most practical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the automatic geometric processing chain can be successfully extended to VHR multispectral images and that the geometric corrections module can be applied to a variety of image data types and sensors.
the automatic processing chain STORM can be successfully applied to VHR multispectral images and delivers high quality products in a fast and cost-effective manner.
automatic image processing can be performed on a routine basis and with near-pixel accuracy on VHR multispectral satellite data.
